what: THE ONE PLACE THE PROJECT'S EXPECTED CHECK AND FAILURE COUNTS LIVE. Written at Batch DE. `check_de.gd` reads this after every battery and reports; `docs/state.md` and `CLAUDE.md` POINT AT IT AND DO NOT RESTATE IT, because a second copy of a number is this project's oldest recurring defect.
how_a_row_moves: A BASELINE MOVES ONLY IN THE BATCH THAT CAUSES THE MOVEMENT, AND THE CHANGELOG SAYS WHY. Otherwise the table drifts into whatever the code happens to do.

fields.kind: suite | gate | scene | harness — chooses how the log is parsed.
fields.checks: [lo, hi] expected check count, or null when the target reports no readable count. THE FLOOR IS ASSERTED AND THE CEILING IS NOT: a FALLING count is an error, a RISING one is a notice.
fields.fails: [lo, hi] expected FAILURE count, or null when unreadable. THE POLARITY INVERTS: a RISING failure count is an error (the 48th failure among 47), a FALLING one is a notice.
fields.checks_obs / fails_obs: HOW MANY READINGS THE ROW RESTS ON. A band is a claim about a distribution nobody has characterised and the readings behind it are part of the claim — an's nine-observation band was exceeded on its tenth. THE COUNTING RULE: one per battery reading the record names from DC forward, plus DE's THREE (before on unmodified HEAD, after, and the final acceptance run) = 6, with named exceptions counted low where there is any doubt. A row whose FAILURE evidence differs from its CHECK evidence carries its own number — see test_batch_bo and test_rune_battle.
fields.expect: optional: a verdict substring that must appear, for a target that reports no counts at all.
fields.flake: optional: a KNOWN flake and its observed rate. Its failure count is carried as a band for that reason.
fields.note: optional: why this row is what it is.

WHEELING CUT deliberately does NOT join: it deals real AoE damage and Break, so a recast is never wasted however long its grant has left, which is why no damaging card is in that list. **BATCH DS: 301 -> 321.** Four of the six new Hunter cards join `RECAST_GATED` (Bear the Brunt, Dug In, Thick Hide, Salve — each is entirely a status on the caster, so a recast buys nothing but a duration the card never promised). BRING IT DOWN deliberately does NOT join: its number is snapshot off the deepest bond's Loyalty, which is uncapped, so a recast on a deeper bond genuinely buys a bigger party-wide amp. HEADS DOWN is not in the system at all — it deals damage, and no damaging card is in that list. **THIS GATE CAUGHT A REAL FAULT BEFORE THE BATTERY**: Salve's `_recast_writes` first proposed the PERFECT's four turns while `check_co` saturates at grade "good", which writes three — so the proposal improved on what was standing every time and the card never refused. The rule it produced is in CLAUDE.md: a proposal must equal what a GOOD cast writes.

COUNTED LOW ON PURPOSE: one reading supports the 43, and the 54 it replaces rested on three.

check_dk.note: NEW AT DK. THE GATE FOR “four ally-worded effects reach the beast, and seven say hero because they cannot”. DJ §2 swept eleven ally-worded effects walking bare `heroes` and ruled on none; DK ruled, and they split FOUR and SEVEN. §1 pins BOTH populations by their own read lines and asserts each in the direction that can break it — a widened site going back to bare `heroes` is a REGRESSION, and a narrow site widening makes its `hero` text wrong. THE RULING IS PINNED AS THAT MEASUREMENT rather than as an assertion, so the day `_companion_hit` grows an `empower` read the gate says the ruling is stale instead of staying quietly true. §5 asserts the eleven texts — seven `hero`, four `ally` — in both directions, plus that no §2 text still carries its pre-DK wording. §6 asserts CV §4's false test is gone from CLAUDE.md, that master.html no longer flags Hold the Line as excluding companions, and that the glossary no longer lists Tank and Spank's Empower as an `ally` effect. THE ±10% DAMAGE ROLL ALONE DOES NOT EXPLAIN 2.40 — modelled over 200,000 trials, ten summed casts a side put the 5th-95th percentile at 2.08-2.26 and P(over the 2.35 ceiling) at 0.1%, about one run in a thousand. A model carrying the FULL differential over-predicts (32% red against 1 in 18 observed), so the live term is smaller than that and larger than zero, and ITS SIZE IS NOT ESTABLISHED — do not guess it. THE FIX IS THE DD SHAPE, WHICH DD APPLIED TWICE IN THIS SUITE AND DID NOT REACH THIS ONE: seed both blows of the compared pair, or set crit_bonus back as the file's own comment says checks that care must do. DO NOT WIDEN THE BAND — the band IS the question. test_batch_bo.note: BATCH DT SEEDED §5's NULL FIELD PAIR AND THE ROW IS NO LONGER FLAKY — `flake` REMOVED AND THE FAILURE CEILING TIGHTENED 1 -> 0, WHICH IS HOW THE FIX GETS ENFORCED. The suite called `seed()` ZERO times; `_nf_seeded()` is now called immediately before EACH of the two compared blows with the same constant, so both arms draw one identical stream and the only difference left between them is the Resonance stack count. PER-PAIR AND NOT PER-SUITE: the other 1104 checks keep their own draw, because widening the seed changes what the rest of the file measures and the BAND IS THE QUESTION. THE EVIDENCE IS DETERMINISM RATHER THAN SAMPLE SIZE, which is why `fails_obs` is only 7: six direct readings plus DT's battery, but the compared pair now reads 17 against 10 on EVERY run where before the seed it ranged shallow 18/16/23/18/28/17 against deep 10/10/11/11/9/10. AND THE DOCUMENTED CAUSE WAS INCOMPLETE, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX: the recorded reason was the ±10% damage roll alone, and a ±10% roll on a mean of 18 spans 16.4-19.8 and CANNOT REACH 28 — a crit is x1.5 and reaches exactly there. So this was `at`'s shape, a second and larger coin hiding behind a variance roll that was taking all the blame, and it is precisely why a per-pair seed was the right instrument: it neutralises every coin at once without anyone having to identify which one was biting. A widened band would have had to be widened to fit a crit, and that band is the assertion. THE CHECK COUNT DOES NOT MOVE (1106) — the change is four lines of code, proven with a comment-stripped diff against HEAD: a two-line helper and its two call sites. The row moved in the batch that caused it. **BATCH DS: 1070 -> 1106.** Its §5 per-card loop checks SIX things about every spec draft-pool entry and its §4 loop one more, and DS adds six cards to three Hunter pools at once. **THE RATE WAS DERIVED BEFORE THE RUN FROM DR'S OWN MOVEMENT** (net +1 card moved this row +6) and the prediction was exact.

test_rune_battle.note: FOUND BY `check_de` ON ITS FIRST ACCEPTANCE RUN AND PREVIOUSLY UNRECORDED. Its CHECK count is rock steady at 97 across all 15 readings — only the failure moves, which is the flake signature CLAUDE.md names. READINGS: clean in DE's before- and after-batteries, RED in the final acceptance battery, RED on the next ad-hoc run, then TEN CONSECUTIVE CLEAN runs on an idle machine. BOTH REDS LANDED UNDER LOAD, which is a hypothesis and not a finding — the assertion's own comment says the snapshot 'is the one that cannot race', so a race is the thing to look at first. THE FIX IS THE `at`/`bo` SHAPE (seed the draw, or assert on the snapshot alone) AND IT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT FOR ITS OWN BATCH: one flake at a time is how the effect stays attributable. SEEDED AT DF §0, per-site: `_seeded()` immediately before the forced hit and nowhere else, so the other 96 checks keep their own stream. THE BAND IS DELIBERATELY NOT TIGHTENED — two clean post-seed readings cannot retire a rate measured over fifteen, and tightening on that evidence is the same fault as writing a band from too few readings, in the opposite direction. The failure message now carries the state the forced hit happened in (battle_over, both units' liveness, the target's fire resist, the pierce fraction), so the NEXT red says what was missing instead of only that it was missing.

check_do.note: BATCH DO's gate. **IT ASSERTS THE PROPERTY AND PRINTS THE COUNT, AND THAT ORDER IS THE WHOLE LESSON OF DN** — DN's own gate asserted a NUMBER and its first battery caught it, costing a second thirty-five-minute frozen run. §1 asserts that NO talent node grants an ability and that NO node names an ability outside its spec's PROTECTED CORE, resolving same-tree names before the global corpus and matching on word boundaries (the `wd_spiked`/Spite and Berserk/Berserker traps), and prints 324 / 0 / 98 / 1 / 0 beside them. §2 asserts each of the twenty-two moved cards drafts from exactly ONE spec pool and resolves, and that NO pool entry anywhere resolves to nothing — the sharp half, because eight of the sixteen relocated definitions were reachable only through `pool_ability`'s fall-through to the trees, so a missed relocation would silently have emptied a `SPEC_POOLS` entry the zone boss offers. §3 asserts all twenty-five re-authored cells are in their ORIGINAL lane and row (`cells_spent` prices off the row, and DN measured a MOVE driving a Berserker ledger to -2 available points, silently), and that the three cut payload terms are absent from the whole of `scripts/` — COMMENT LINES STRIPPED FIRST, because a comment recording a cut necessarily NAMES what was cut, and that fired during DO's own control run. §4 is a REPORT: it prints every node reading a status its own spec cannot guarantee (twelve pairs, six of them DO's own) and asserts only `sm_precision`, which §3 of the brief singled out. §5 asserts the standing rule is written down. **IT NEEDS NO `check_da` WALK_EXEMPT ENTRY**: it reads only the SPEC draft pool, never the class one, so §3's two-call fingerprint does not match — and its header does not NAME the forbidden call either, which it did in its first draft and went 37/2 on. EIGHT NEGATIVE CONTROLS WERE RUN AND ALL EIGHT BIT: the three cut terms restored (1 failure each), a grant put back on `ar_wrath` (2), a cell MOVED from row 3 to row 7 (1), `sm_precision`'s Dazed restored (4), Backdraft pulled from its draft pool (1 here and 4 in check_cz), and a deliberate syntax error in `relics.gd` (26 Parse Errors on the check_parse stderr grep, 0 once reverted).

check_dp.note: BATCH DP's gate, and it extends `check_do` rather than repeating it: the ability rule and the STATUS rule are the same rule, and DO's ability-matching instrument could not see this class of bet at all (`sm_precision` named no ability and was still a bet). §1 sweeps every node's rendered text against every status form and ASSERTS THE PROPERTY, printing 324 / 6 / 6 / 0 beside it. **THE RATCHET IS ASYMMETRIC ON PURPOSE, which is this file's own rule one layer up**: a pair NOT in `KNOWN_PAIRS` is an ERROR (a new bet), a known pair that has GONE is a NOTICE (a repair) — a gate that reds on a repair teaches the next batch to leave the defect alone. **IT READS `check_do`'s `GUARANTEED_STATUS` AND `STATUS_FORMS` RATHER THAN COPYING THEM**, and asserts the load, because a second copy of a hand-authored table is this project's oldest recurring defect. §2 asserts the four re-pointed cells are in their ORIGINAL lane and row, name Ruin, and read FOUR DISTINCT quantities — an application, its magnitude, an event and a depth threshold — because four cells all reading 'stacks of Ruin' would flatten a lane authored as a theme; none reads a DETONATION, which Grim Focus, Unraveling and Avatar of Ruin already own. §3 asserts the six new read sites exist, the four old ones are GONE (a field read in two places under two meanings is a silent order-dependence), that `permanent_delusion` is absent from `scripts/` WITH COMMENT LINES STRIPPED FIRST (DO's scar — prose recording a removal necessarily names what was removed), and that no `_gain_ruin` call quotes `OLD_GODS_MARK` directly, so a sixth passive site cannot be added that Whispers silently fails to reach. §4 is the check that would have caught the cost this batch nearly paid: **every stat field any rune writes has a live read site in `scripts/`** (116 fields across 65 runes, 0 dead) — the Rune of the Whispering Dark writes `spread_ranks` AND `spread_ruin`, so a fresh field name would have left two of its four clauses paying nothing in silence. §5 asserts every rune grant still RESOLVES (a rune grant goes through `Classes.pending_talent_ability`, not the draft resolver, so DO moving card NAMES while DEFINITIONS stayed put is the only reason four granting runes still work) and REPORTS the two that now duplicate a draft card's grant. §6 asserts the standing rule is written down. **IT NEEDS NO `check_da` WALK_EXEMPT ENTRY**: it reads only the SPEC draft pool, and its header does not name the other call either. NINE NEGATIVE CONTROLS WERE RUN AND ALL NINE BEHAVED: the four cells' old texts restored (5, 5, 6, 6 failures), the Ruined Mind read site defeated (3), the Whispering Dark's `spread_ruin` renamed (5), a sixth `_gain_ruin` call made to quote the constant (3) — and **the comment-stripping trap controlled from BOTH sides**: `permanent_delusion` as a COMMENT left it GREEN, the same identifier as CODE turned it RED.

check_ds.note: NEW AT DT. THE GATE FOR THE TWO DS SPECIALS THAT SHIPPED WITH NO PERMANENT LIVE COVERAGE. DS authored six Hunter cards and added no gate; `check_co`'s saturation sweep reaches four of the six as a side effect and `bring_it_down` and `heads_down` were covered by nothing at all. Both WERE driven at DS in a scratch fixture that is not in the repo (`ds_live.gd`, untracked), and that throwaway run is what found the `cost > 0` fault; this is its permanent copy. IT SPAWNS TWICE AND THAT IS FORCED: `Gate.spawn` fields ONE hunter slot and the two cards belong to two different Hunter specs, so a Beastmaster fixture and a Sharpshooter fixture are both required (`check_di` is the precedent). §0 derives the enemy corpus on every run rather than quoting it — 50 abilities across 21 kits, 46 free, and 14 of the 21 KITS carry a zero-cost damaging ability that is not the basic — and asserts a RATIO (>=90% free) rather than a literal, so it stays true as enemies are authored and goes red if the mana premise ever becomes live. §1 IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED, because BRING IT DOWN is stamped in one place and read three thousand lines away, which is exactly DK's Empower shape: 10 seeded Warden strikes read 8526 plain against 10233 under the capped +20%, ratio 1.2002 against a wanted 1.2000. IT ALSO PINS the snapshot, the cap, the no-bond refusal, that the bond is not spent, and that the BEAST does not wear the amp it earned — the walk is `heroes`, which is the one property the card text does not state and the handler does. A THIRD ARM STRIPS THE AMP FROM THE STRIKER ALONE while the party keeps it and requires the ratio back at 1.0; THE NEGATIVE CONTROL THAT REPLACED THE PER-WEARER READ WITH A PARTY-WIDE GLOBAL PASSED BOTH OTHER ARMS AND FAILED ONLY THAT ONE, which is why it is not decoration. §2c IS THE POINT OF THE GATE AND IS THE ONE ASSERTION A STATIC CHECK COULD NOT MAKE. Both versions of Heads Down refuse abilities, name a criterion and log a fallback; the only thing that separates the shipped identity test against `_cheapest_attack` from the `cost > 0` fault is HOW MANY REFUSED ABILITIES COST NOTHING. Positive under identity on 14 of 21 kits; zero under a cost test on all but two. The gate walks a live kit through `_intent_ability_usable` and asserts that count is positive. It also asserts the fallback cannot be starved, drives the downgrade through `_revalidate_intent` (returns the basic, `intent_fallback` +1), lands it on an UNBROKEN BOSS live rather than re-pinning `_apply_status`'s carve-out literal that two suites already pin, and asserts `_choose_enemy_action` contains no `heads_down` read at all (BL §1's promise, in the direction that can break it). FOUR NEGATIVE CONTROLS AND ALL FOUR BIT: the cost test restored (6 failures, the raider reading "2 kept, 0 refused"), the `heroes` walk widened to `_hero_side()` (1), the strike-site read deleted (1, ratio 1.0000 — DK's defect exactly), and the per-wearer read made global (1, caught by the third arm alone). `battle.gd` was backed up to scratch and restored by `cp` after each, never by `git checkout`, and the md5 verified identical all four times. IT NEEDS NO `check_da` §3 EXEMPTION AND IT TOOK A RED TO ESTABLISH THAT: the gate calls neither draft-pool accessor, but its HEADER COMMENT named both fingerprint strings while explaining that it does not, and §3 matches on substrings. The names came out of the prose rather than an exemption being granted — an exemption granted to a sentence blinds the rule to a real walk arriving in that file later. Gate takes ~25s. ONE READING SUPPORTS THE 57.
